disease_label_per_paper: Infant acute myocarditis mimicking acute myocardial infarction
presentation_summary: 9-month-old girl with recent rhinorrhea and cough was brought to the pediatric emergency department for sudden dyspnea.
Exam showed acute heart failure with pulse 180/min, blood pressure 70/40 mmHg, respiratory rate 48/min, chest indrawing, and temperature 38.9 C.
Admission ECG showed ventricular tachycardia that spontaneously returned to a regular rhythm with extrasystoles.
Chest radiograph showed cardiomegaly with bilateral pulmonary congestion.
Troponin I rose from 0.81 to 1.92 ng/mL, CK rose to 2066 U/L, and ECG after 3 hours showed anterolateral ST elevation with reciprocal depression.
